title: Add per-tenant KV cache span metrics and redesign console dashboards after capacity-induced outage
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Follow-up ticket from a capacity event on 2026-02-08 where Console dashboards lost KV cache visibility. Root cause: missing per-tenant KV cache span instrumentation and an aggregation bug in the metrics pipeline that dropped low-cardinality span tags. This made it impossible to attribute tail-latency to cache behavior during the outage.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-08 a capacity spike caused increased cache evictions. Console dashboards showed generic request latency increases but lacked cache-hit/miss signals and per-tenant kv_cache metrics, preventing rapid triage. Tracing omitted kv_cache spans for LRU evictions due to a recent tracer change that stripped span attribute propagation.
timeline: 2026-02-08 03:12: Capacity spike detected; console global latency axis increased
2026-02-08 03:18: Alerts fired for p95 latency; SREs began Triage
2026-02-08 03:45: Engineers noted dashboards lacked kv_cache hit/miss and per-tenant heatmaps
2026-02-08 04:02: Temporary mitigation: increased cache size and enabled emergency routing to Dedicated
2026-02-09 09:00: Post-incident review with engineering, product, and SREs
action_items: Add per-tenant kv_cache.metrics: hit_count, miss_count, evictions, lookup_duration_ms (histogram)
Instrument KV cache L1/L2 eviction spans with attributes: tenant_id, cache_key_prefix, eviction_reason
Fix metrics pipeline to preserve low-cardinality span tags and ensure tenant_id is not dropped
Design and ship Console dashboards: per-tenant kv_cache hitratio heatmap, per-route cache impact overlay, and tail-latency waterfall with cache span annotations
Create synthetic checks that exercise cache read/write and assert expected hitratio baseline daily
Update runbook to include cache-metric checks, and add playbook steps for emergency capacity adjustments
Add alert: per-tenant kv_cache.eviction_rate > threshold AND p95 latency delta > X for 5m
decisions: Prefer shallow histogram for lookup_duration_ms to limit cardinality and avoid high-series explosion
Emit tenant_id as a limited set label (hash prefix) to protect PII and reduce cardinality
Dashboards will default to aggregated view with ability to filter to a tenant; per-tenant defaults hidden behind an RBAC toggle
blockers: Metrics pipeline change requires coordination with infra team owning metrics-ingest (INC-ops)
Need a small SLO budget increase to enable synthetic checks in production observability tier
review_feedback: PM requested that dashboards surface potential customer impact buckets (High/Medium/Low) for easier ops prioritization (link to mockups)
Design asked for colorblind-friendly palette for heatmaps and requested a compact 'summary row' for per-tenant list
SREs emphasized adding an automated rollback for instrumentation if it causes cardinality blowup
acceptance_criteria: Console shows per-tenant kv_cache.hit_rate and eviction_rate in release-2026.03
Tracing captures kv_cache eviction spans and they appear in distributed trace view with tenant_id label
Synthetic cache check runs successfully for 7 days with stable baseline and alerting enabled
No unbounded increase in metric series cardinality after rollout (monitoring alert for cardinality)
notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to instrumentation and dashboarding. Separate follow-ups will cover long-term cache eviction remediation and autoscaler tuning.
Keep stakeholders (PM: Jonah Lee, Design: Priya Desai, SRE lead: Maria Lopez) on weekly updates until done
